grand_strategy.reading: Solomon Islands sells its logs mostly to China and borrows from it, while its police and security are shared out between Beijing (the 2022 pact and the 2023 policing deal) and Canberra (the 2017 treaty and the A$190 million package of December 2024). Its leverage is the forum it hosted in 2025: as Pacific Islands Forum host it kept every dialogue partner out, and the CSIS analysis reads that compromise as shaped by Chinese pressure, with Taiwan among the excluded. The Manele government, which had resisted closer ties with Australia, fell by no-confidence vote; Matthew Wale took office on 15 May 2026, calls the China pact under review and seeks a comprehensive strategic treaty with Australia, while the July 2026 shiprider deal with the US shows a government that no longer wants to choose one patron.

stances.note: A bilateral security treaty (August 2017, after RAMSI ended in 2017) makes this an alignment, with visible friction: DFAT lists several disagreements, including the Julian Moti affair and the 2022 Chinese security pact, and AP reported that Manele resisted closer ties. Warming since the December 2024 police package (announced, not signed, per the PM transcript) and the June 2026 Wale-Albanese agreement to negotiate a comprehensive strategic treaty, which both governments called a reset. Bond none: no shared identity or open wound is cited in these sources; RAMSI is not treated as a grievance here.

stances.note: No alliance. Leader-level talks in August 2025 and updated border frameworks finalised in Honiara in September 2025, which keep traditional rights for border communities. Bond kin is our reading: the border is shared by communities, and the Choiseul provincial premier has said his province intends to join PNG autonomous region once Bougainville becomes a state, so the Melanesian neighbour is not treated as foreign. The sources do not use the word kin (confidence C). Bougainville leaders recommended 1 September 2030 as the independence date in July 2026; that question stays with PNG.

stances.note: Argued grade: not an ally, although the 2022 security pact is a treaty. Its text was not published, and the Wale government (since 15 May 2026) has said it will review the pact under a nondisclosure clause. The 2023 police deal and the US$66 million Huawei loan are transactional. Beijing calls the policing cooperation a positive contribution and says it will work with the new government; that is rhetoric, so it does not move the grade. Bond none: no kinship, no sympathy cited in sources (the "look north" policy is in the index only, so affinity is not recorded). Trend cooling from the change of government. The since date follows the September 2019 switch from Taipei. CSIS calls China the closest security partner (via the Business Standard mirror).

stances.note: Transactional. The US embassy in Honiara reopened in early 2023 (official effective date 27 January, public ceremony 2 February), framed by Washington as a response to China. The shiprider agreement signed in Honiara in late July 2026 lets Solomon officers board designated US Coast Guard vessels in the EEZ; the government says it has no nondisclosure clause and the text will be published, and the opposition leader Manasseh Sogavare says it could compromise sovereignty. stances_toward.note: Partner on trial: Australia has had a bilateral security agreement with Honiara since 2017 (after the RAMSI years), but the 2022 China-Solomons policing pact is the standing problem - the Global Initiative found in May 2026 that the Solomons had 'emerged as China's most prominent policing partner in the Pacific'. The new prime minister, Matthew Wale, promised to review the pact and 'reset' relations; Wale was due to meet Albanese in early June 2026, when the two were to commit to elevate the relationship in a new comprehensive treaty at Honiara's request (a Solomon Islands minister suggested end-2026 for the announcement) and to sign an MoU for a A$190m police package. Not signed as of our last source; warming on the reset. Bond - affinity: Australia led the regional mission in the Solomons (Wikipedia index); no source found on how Honiara frames it.
